results.title: Comparison theorem
results.label: thm:comparison
results.statement:
\label{thm:comparison}
Let $\mathscr R$ be a recursion category with ranges and binary
restriction coproducts, let $\mathcal A$ be a restriction category with
ranges, restriction zeros, and binary restriction coproducts, and let
$F:\mathscr R\to\mathcal A$ be a range functor.
Choose a Turing morphism $\tau:U\times U\rightharpoonup U$ and an
isomorphism $b:U\to U+U$. Define
\[
 h=b\tau\Delta_U:U\rightharpoonup U+U,\qquad
 a_0=h^*(1_U+0_U),\qquad a_1=h^*(0_U+1_U).
\]
Let $P,N$ be disjoint restriction idempotents on $FU$ such that
$F(a_0)\le P$ and $F(a_1)\le N$. Suppose that
$s:FU\rightharpoonup FU+FU$ satisfies
\[
 s^*(1_{FU}+0_{FU})=N,\qquad
 s^*(0_{FU}+1_{FU})=P,
\]
and that there is a morphism $\ell:U\rightharpoonup U+U$ with
$F\ell=\chi_{U,U}s$.
Then there is a total morphism $g:U\to U$ such that
\[
 (Fg)^*P=(Fg)^*N=0_{FU}.
\]
If $F(1_U)\ne0$ and inverse image along $Fg$ preserves the join
$P\vee N$, then $P\vee N\ne1_{FU}$.
results.proof:
Put $u=b^{-1}\ell:U\rightharpoonup U$. Apply the Turing property
to $u\pi_2:U\times U\rightharpoonup U$, obtaining a total morphism
$g:U\to U$ with $\tau(g\times1_U)=u\pi_2$.
Precomposition with $\langle1_U,g\rangle:U\to U\times U$ gives
$\tau\Delta_Ug=ug$, and therefore $hg=\ell g$.

Write
$E=Fg:FU\to FU$ and
$H=\chi_{U,U}^{-1}Fh:FU\rightharpoonup FU+FU$.
Applying $F$ to the preceding identity gives $HE=sE$.
The coproduct comparison identifies the images of the source summand
idempotents with the target summand idempotents. Preservation of
restrictions and composition therefore gives
\[
 E^*F(a_0)=E^*N,\qquad E^*F(a_1)=E^*P.
\]
The inequalities imply
\[
 E^*N=E^*F(a_0)\le E^*P,\qquad
 E^*P=E^*F(a_1)\le E^*N.
\]
The two inverse images are equal, and their meet is
$E^*(PN)=0_{FU}$. Hence both are zero.
If $P\vee N=1_{FU}$, totality of $E$ and preservation of this join
would give
\[
 1_{FU}=E^*1_{FU}=E^*(P\vee N)
       =E^*P\vee E^*N=0_{FU},
\]
contrary to $F(1_U)\ne0$.
hypotheses_used: Source Turing property and isomorphism b; target restriction, zeros, coproducts; F preserves restrictions, ranges, zeros and coproducts; disjoint P,N and bounds; lifted switched conditional; final nonzero and join-preservation hypotheses only for noncoverage.
proof_reconstruction: Apply source parameterization to b⁻¹ℓπ₂:U×U⇀U and precompose with ⟨1_U,g⟩, obtaining hg=ℓg.
Apply F and its coproduct comparison to identify (Fg)*F(a₀)=(Fg)*N and (Fg)*F(a₁)=(Fg)*P.
The bounding inequalities force the latter two inverse images to coincide; their meet is the inverse image of PN=0, so both vanish.
If P∨N=1, totality and the explicitly assumed preservation of that join force 1_FU=0.

results.title: Lifted separators
results.label: cor:separator
results.statement:
\label{cor:separator}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison} on
$\mathscr R$, $\mathcal A$, $F$, $\tau$, and $b$, suppose that
$F(1_U)\ne0$ and inverse images along total morphisms in $\mathcal A$ preserve
binary joins. A complementary pair $P,N$ on $FU$ satisfying
$F(a_0)\le P$ and $F(a_1)\le N$ admits no pair of morphisms
$s:FU\rightharpoonup FU+FU$ and
$\ell:U\rightharpoonup U+U$ with
\[
 s^*(1_{FU}+0_{FU})=N,\qquad
 s^*(0_{FU}+1_{FU})=P,\qquad
 F\ell=\chi_{U,U}s.
\]
results.proof:
Such morphisms would give $P\vee N\ne1_{FU}$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison}, contradicting complementarity.
hypotheses_used: Exactly Theorem 3.1 hypotheses plus complementarity and total inverse-image preservation of binary joins.
proof_reconstruction: The alleged s,ℓ satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1.
Its noncoverage conclusion contradicts P∨N=1.
No product preservation by F is used.

results.title: Inseparability from complementary conditionals
results.label: cor:source-conditionals
results.statement:
\label{cor:source-conditionals}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison} on
$\mathscr R$, $\mathcal A$, $F$, $\tau$, and $b$, suppose that
$F(1_U)\ne0$ and inverse images along total morphisms in $\mathcal A$ preserve
binary joins of restriction idempotents.
Suppose that, for every complementary pair $c,c'$ on $U$, there
is a total morphism $\ell_c:U\to U+U$ satisfying
\[
 \ell_cc=i_1c,\qquad \ell_cc'=i_0c',
\]
where $i_0,i_1:U\to U+U$ are the coproduct injections.
Then the restriction idempotents $a_0,a_1$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison} are inseparable in $\mathscr R$.
results.proof:
Put $\varepsilon_0=1_U+0_U$ and $\varepsilon_1=0_U+1_U$.
The morphisms $\varepsilon_0\ell_c$ and $i_0c'$ agree after
composition with both $c$ and $c'$. Hence they agree after
$[c,c']:U+U\rightharpoonup U$. Its range is
$c\vee c'=1_U$, so the agreement law for ranges gives
$\varepsilon_0\ell_c=i_0c'$.
The same argument gives $\varepsilon_1\ell_c=i_1c$.
Taking restrictions yields $\ell_c^*\varepsilon_0=c'$ and
$\ell_c^*\varepsilon_1=c$.

If $c,c'$ separated $a_0,a_1$, put $P=F(c)$ and $N=F(c')$.
These are complementary target restriction idempotents.
For the canonical coproduct isomorphism
$\chi_{U,U}:FU+FU\to F(U+U)$, define
$s_c=\chi_{U,U}^{-1}F(\ell_c):FU\to FU+FU$.
Restriction preservation and the coproduct comparison give
\[
 s_c^*(1_{FU}+0_{FU})=N,\qquad
 s_c^*(0_{FU}+1_{FU})=P.
\]
Together with $F(\ell_c)=\chi_{U,U}s_c$, these identities contradict
Corollary~\ref{cor:separator}.
hypotheses_used: Theorem 3.1 data; total conditional for every complementary pair on U; target joins and nonzero identity.
proof_reconstruction: The conditional branch equations give ε₀ℓ_c=i₀c′ and ε₁ℓ_c=i₁c after precomposition with c,c′.
The agreement law cancels their copairing because ran[c,c′]=c∨c′=1.
Restrictions then give exactly the switched inverse-image equations.
A hypothetical source separator is sent by F to a complementary target separator, contradicting Corollary 3.2.

results.label: prop:disjoint-joins
results.statement:
\label{prop:disjoint-joins}
Let $\mathcal C$ be a restriction category with restriction zeros and
binary restriction coproducts. Suppose every pair of parallel morphisms
whose restriction idempotents are disjoint has a join in the restriction
order.
For complementary restriction idempotents $c,c'$ on $X$, the morphism
\[
 \ell_c=(i_1c)\vee(i_0c'):X\rightharpoonup X+X
\]
is total and satisfies $\ell_cc=i_1c$ and $\ell_cc'=i_0c'$.
results.proof:
The restrictions of $i_1c$ and $i_0c'$ are $c$ and $c'$ because
the injections are total. The upper-bound equations for the join
give $\ell_cc=i_1c$ and $\ell_cc'=i_0c'$.
Both $c$ and $c'$ lie below $\bar\ell_c$, so
$1_X=c\vee c'\le\bar\ell_c$ and $\ell_c$ is total.
hypotheses_used: Restriction zeros, coproducts with total injections, existence of joins for parallel morphisms with disjoint restrictions.
proof_reconstruction: The restrictions of i₁c and i₀c′ are c and c′.
Join upper-bound equations give the two prescribed branch values.
Both c,c′ lie below the restriction of the join, and c∨c′=1 forces totality.

results.title: Interpretation of a sentence theory
results.label: prop:interpreted-theory
results.statement:
\label{prop:interpreted-theory}
Let $F:\mathscr R\to\mathcal A$ be a range functor with split
target, let $\widehat F:\Split(\mathscr R)\to\mathcal A$ be the
extension by chosen splittings, and let $t_A=m_A r_A=\ran(c_{A,S})$
be a sentence theory constructed above. Then
\begin{gather*}
 \widehat F(t_A)=\ran(\widehat F(c_{A,S})),\\
 \widehat F(m_A)\widehat F(r_A)=\widehat F(t_A),\qquad
 \widehat F(r_A)\widehat F(m_A)=1_{\widehat F(T_{A,S})}.
\end{gather*}
Suppose moreover that $\mathcal A=\Par(\mathcal E,\Mono)$ for a
regular category $\mathcal E$. If the total morphism
$\widehat F(c_{A,S})$ factors in $\mathcal E$ through a
monomorphism $v:V\hookrightarrow\widehat F S$, then
$\widehat F(m_A)$ is a subobject of $v$. Put
\[
 d_V=[\widehat F S\xleftarrow{v}V\xrightarrow{v}\widehat F S]:
 \widehat F S\rightharpoonup\widehat F S.
\]
If $d_V(\widehat F\nu)^*d_V=0$, then
$\widehat F(t_A)(\widehat F\nu)^*\widehat F(t_A)=0$.
results.proof:
Range preservation gives the first equation, and functoriality
gives the two splitting equations. In $\Par(\mathcal E,\Mono)$,
every monomorphism of $\mathcal E$ has a partial inverse.
Lemma~\ref{lem:range-regular-image} therefore identifies the range
of $\widehat F(c_{A,S})$ with the partial identity on its regular
image in $\mathcal E$. Its splitting by $\widehat F(m_A)$ and
$\widehat F(r_A)$ identifies $\widehat F(m_A)$ with that image.
Factorization through $v$ implies
$\widehat F(t_A)\le d_V$. Monotonicity of inverse image and meet
then gives
\[
 \widehat F(t_A)(\widehat F\nu)^*\widehat F(t_A)
 \le d_V(\widehat F\nu)^*d_V=0.
\]
hypotheses_used: Chosen-splitting extension of range functor; sentence-range splitting; for final assertion target Par(E,Mono) with E regular and validity factorization.
proof_reconstruction: Functoriality carries both splitting equations; range preservation carries t_A=ran(c_A,S).
In Par(E,Mono), Lemma A.7 identifies the range with the regular image.
Factorization of the conclusion through v bounds the interpreted theorem domain by d_V.
Monotonicity of inverse image and meet transfers d_V∧(Fν)*d_V=0 to the interpreted domain.

results.label: thm:logical-comparison
results.statement:
\label{thm:logical-comparison}
Let $\mathscr R,\mathcal A,F,U,\tau,b,a_0,a_1$ satisfy the
categorical hypotheses and definitions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison}. Suppose that $\mathcal A$ is split,
that inverse images along total morphisms in $\mathcal A$ preserve binary joins
of restriction idempotents, and that $F(1_U)\ne0$.
Let $t_A=\ran(c_{A,S})$ represent a sentence theory in
$\Split(\mathscr R)$ as above, with total negation
$\nu:S\to S$, and let $\theta:U\to S$ be total in
$\Split(\mathscr R)$. Put
\[
 t=\widehat F(t_A),\qquad
 P=(\widehat F\theta)^*t,\qquad
 N=(\widehat F\theta)^*(\widehat F\nu)^*t.
\]
Assume that $t(\widehat F\nu)^*t=0$, $F(a_0)\le P$, and
$F(a_1)\le N$.
Suppose there are partial morphisms
$s:FU\rightharpoonup FU+FU$ and
$\ell:U\rightharpoonup U+U$ satisfying
\[
 s^*(1_{FU}+0_{FU})=N,\qquad
 s^*(0_{FU}+1_{FU})=P,\qquad
 F\ell=\chi_{U,U}s.
\]
Then there is a total $g:U\to U$ in $\mathscr R$ such that
\[
 (\widehat F(\theta g))^*t=0,\qquad
 (\widehat F(\theta g))^*(\widehat F\nu)^*t=0.
\]
In particular,
\[
 t\vee(\widehat F\nu)^*t\ne1_{\widehat F S},\qquad
 t_A\vee\nu^*t_A\ne1_S.
\]
results.proof:
Preservation of meets and zero by inverse image gives
$PN=(\widehat F\theta)^*\bigl(t(\widehat F\nu)^*t\bigr)=0$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison} therefore supplies a total $g:U\to U$
with $(Fg)^*P=(Fg)^*N=0$. Since $\widehat F$ agrees with $F$ on
$\mathscr R$, composition of inverse images gives the two equalities.

If $t\vee(\widehat F\nu)^*t=1_{\widehat F S}$, inverse image along
the total morphism $\widehat F(\theta g):FU\to\widehat F S$ would
give
\[
 1_{FU}
 =(\widehat F(\theta g))^*\bigl(t\vee(\widehat F\nu)^*t\bigr)
 =0\vee0=0,
\]
contrary to $F(1_U)\ne0$.
If $t_A\vee\nu^*t_A=1_S$, applying $\widehat F$ and using
preservation of joins and inverse images would give
$t\vee(\widehat F\nu)^*t=1_{\widehat F S}$, a contradiction.
hypotheses_used: Theorem 3.1 data; split target; θ total; semantic consistency; both diagonal bounds and lifted switched conditional; total inverse images preserve binary joins; nonzero identity.
proof_reconstruction: Pull back semantic consistency along F̂θ to get PN=0.
Theorem 3.1 supplies total g and zero inverse images of both pulled-back domains.
Compose inverse-image identities to obtain both asserted equalities for F̂(θg).
A complete interpreted theory would pull back to 1_FU=0; completeness in the source maps to completeness in the target, giving the second contradiction.

results.label: cor:domain-incompleteness
results.statement:
\label{cor:domain-incompleteness}
Let $\mathcal C$ be a restriction category with restriction zeros and
binary joins of restriction idempotents preserved by inverse image along total morphisms.
Let $a,b$ be inseparable restriction idempotents on $U$. Suppose that
$\theta:U\to S$ and $\nu:S\to S$ are total, and that a restriction
idempotent $t_0$ on $S$ satisfies $a\le\theta^*t_0$ and
$b\le\theta^*\nu^*t_0$.
For every restriction idempotent $t\ge t_0$ on $S$ with $t\,\nu^*t=0_S$,
the pair $t,\nu^*t$ is inseparable. In particular,
$t\vee\nu^*t\ne1_S$.
results.proof:
Suppose complementary restriction idempotents $e,e'$ on $S$ satisfy
$t\le e$ and $\nu^*t\le e'$. Put
$c=\theta^*e$ and $c'=\theta^*e'$. Inverse image preserves
meets and zero, so $cc'=\theta^*(ee')=0_U$.
Preservation of joins and totality of $\theta$ give
$c\vee c'=\theta^*(e\vee e')=\theta^*1_S=1_U$.
Monotonicity gives
$a\le\theta^*t_0\le\theta^*t\le c$ and
$b\le\theta^*\nu^*t_0\le\theta^*\nu^*t\le c'$.
Thus $c,c'$ would separate $a,b$, a contradiction.
If $t\vee\nu^*t=1_S$, the disjoint pair $t,\nu^*t$ would
itself be such a complementary separator.
hypotheses_used: Inseparable pair a,b; total θ and ν; t₀ bounds; total inverse images preserve joins; candidate extension t≥t₀ is consistent.
proof_reconstruction: A complementary separator e,e′ of t,ν*t pulls back along θ to disjoint idempotents.
Totality and join preservation make those pullbacks complementary.
Monotonicity and the t₀ bounds make them a separator of a,b, impossible.
If t∨ν*t=1, the consistent pair itself is such a separator.

results.title: Generation reflection
results.label: thm:first-order-reflection
results.statement:
\label{thm:first-order-reflection}
Under the preceding hypotheses, $\operatorname{Gen}$ is extensive,
monotone, and idempotent. It is left adjoint to the inclusion
$\iota:\operatorname{Th}_{\mathcal D}(S)\hookrightarrow
\operatorname{Sub}_{\mathcal D}(S)$. Thus, for every axiom
subobject $A$ and sentence theory $T$,
\[
 \operatorname{Gen}(A)\leq T\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\leq T.
\]
Let $J:\operatorname{Th}_{\mathcal D}(S)\to\mathcal D/S$ send a
theory to its inclusion. Then
$\Gamma(a:A\to S)=\operatorname{Gen}(\im a)$ defines a functor
$\Gamma:\mathcal D/S\to\operatorname{Th}_{\mathcal D}(S)$ with
$\Gamma\dashv J$.
results.proof:
Axiom introduction gives $A\leq\operatorname{Gen}(A)$, and
leastness of $C(A)$ gives monotonicity. The closed formula
subobject $C(A)$ contains $j_!\operatorname{Gen}(A)$, whence
$C(\operatorname{Gen}(A))\leq C(A)$. Pullback along $j$ and
extensivity prove idempotence. The equivalence follows
from these three properties. A morphism in $\mathcal D/S$ from
$a:A\to S$ to $J(T)$ exists uniquely exactly when $\im a\leq T$.
The equivalence identifies this hom-set with the hom-set from
$\Gamma(a)$ to $T$ in the theory order, naturally in both objects.
hypotheses_used: Regularity; finite disjoint stable coproducts; initial syntax and derivation algebras for each relevant axiom subobject.
proof_reconstruction: Leastness of the generated formula subobject gives extensivity and monotonicity.
C(A) contains j_!Gen(A), so C(Gen(A))≤C(A); restriction to sentences gives idempotence.
For closed T, Gen(A)≤T iff A≤T.
For arbitrary a:A→S, regular image factorization gives Hom_D/S(a,J(T)) either empty or singleton according as im(a)≤T; this is equivalent to Gen(im(a))≤T, naturally.
Only image subobjects need initial derivation algebras; the proof does not assume an initial algebra for the unquotiented axiom morphism a.

results.title: Translation Galois connection
results.label: thm:translation-galois
results.statement:
\label{thm:translation-galois}
Let $\sigma:P\to Q$ be a logical translation between presentations
satisfying the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:first-order-reflection}. Inverse image along
$\sigma_S$ sends sentence theories to sentence theories, and
\[
 \sigma_\#:\operatorname{Th}_P\rightleftarrows
 \operatorname{Th}_Q:\sigma^*,\qquad
 \sigma_\#(T)=\operatorname{Gen}_Q(\sigma_!T),\qquad
 \sigma_\#\dashv\sigma^*.
\]
Here $\sigma_!$ and $\sigma^*$ abbreviate the image and inverse-image
operations for $\sigma_S$. Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{Gen}_Q\sigma_!
   =\sigma_\#\operatorname{Gen}_P.
\]
For composable logical translations $\sigma:P\to Q$ and
$\rho:Q\to R$,
\[
 (\rho\sigma)_\#=\rho_\#\sigma_\#,\qquad
 (\rho\sigma)^*=\sigma^*\rho^*.
\]
results.proof:
If $T$ is a $Q$-theory, $\sigma_{\Phi}^*C_Q(T)$ contains the
logical axioms, is closed under the $P$-rules, and contains
$j_{P,!}\sigma^*T$. Thus
$C_P(\sigma^*T)\leq\sigma_{\Phi}^*C_Q(T)$.
Pullback along $j_P$ gives
$\operatorname{Gen}_P(\sigma^*T)\leq\sigma^*T$;
extensivity gives equality. Now image and inverse image satisfy
$\sigma_!A\leq B$ exactly when $A\leq\sigma^*B$.
Combining this with Theorem~\ref{thm:first-order-reflection}
proves the adjunction.

Apply closure preservation to
$T=\operatorname{Gen}_Q(\sigma_!A)$. The resulting inclusion
$\sigma_!\operatorname{Gen}_P(A)
\leq\operatorname{Gen}_Q(\sigma_!A)$, together with extensivity
and idempotence, proves the generation identity. Composition of
images and pullbacks then gives the two composition identities.
hypotheses_used: Logical translation preserving syntax, admissible substitution and rule instances; generation hypotheses for both presentations.
proof_reconstruction: Pulling C_Q(T) back along σ_Φ gives a P-rule-closed formula subobject containing σ_S*T.
Initiality/leastness bounds C_P(σ*T) by that pullback; restriction to sentences proves inverse-image closure.
The regular-image/pullback Galois correspondence and generation reflection yield σ_#⊣σ*.
Apply closure preservation to Gen_Q(σ_!A), then extensivity and idempotence, to obtain the generation identity.
Composition of images and pullbacks yields both composition identities; these are equalities of subobject classes.

results.title: Comparison of deduction
results.label: prop:deduction-comparison
results.statement:
\label{prop:deduction-comparison}
With these data, suppose that for every $A\hookrightarrow S_1$
there is a total morphism
\[
 p_A:GP_{A,S_1}\to P_{L(A),S_2},\qquad
 c_{L(A),S_2}p_A=\sigma Gc_{A,S_1}.
\]
Then $L^{\mathrm{th}}(T)=\operatorname{Gen}_2L(T)$ defines a
functor on theory orders satisfying
\[
 L^{\mathrm{th}}\operatorname{Gen}_1=\operatorname{Gen}_2L,
 \qquad \Gamma_2K=L^{\mathrm{th}}\Gamma_1.
\]
Consequently the left-adjoint square in
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \mathcal D_1/S_1\arrow[r,"K"]
   \arrow[d,shift right=.8ex,"\Gamma_1"'] &
 \mathcal D_2/S_2\arrow[d,shift right=.8ex,"\Gamma_2"']\\
 \operatorname{Th}_1\arrow[r,"L^{\mathrm{th}}"']
   \arrow[u,shift right=.8ex,"J_1"'] &
 \operatorname{Th}_2\arrow[u,shift right=.8ex,"J_2"']
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad \Gamma_i\dashv J_i
\]
commutes. Factorization through the generated theory gives a natural
transformation $KJ_1\to J_2L^{\mathrm{th}}$.
If $L\dashv R$ on subobject orders, $R$ sends theories to theories
and $L^{\mathrm{th}}\dashv R|_{\operatorname{Th}_2}$.
results.proof:
Taking images of the derivation comparison gives
$L\operatorname{Gen}_1\leq\operatorname{Gen}_2L$.
Apply $\operatorname{Gen}_2$ and use extensivity and idempotence
to obtain the first identity. Regularity identifies the image
of $K(a)$ with $L(\im a)$, proving the second identity.
The unique factorization through that image and its closure defines
the comparison. Uniqueness proves naturality.
For a closed $B$, adjunction gives $LRB\leq B$, and hence
\[
 L\operatorname{Gen}_1(RB)
 \leq\operatorname{Gen}_2(LRB)\leq B.
\]
Thus $\operatorname{Gen}_1(RB)\leq RB$. Extensivity gives
equality, and the restricted adjunction follows from the
generation reflection.
hypotheses_used: G regular; σ:GS₁→S₂ total; each specified p_A commutes with sentence conclusions; optional L⊣R for the final assertion.
proof_reconstruction: The commuting p_A gives LGen₁(A)≤Gen₂L(A) after taking regular images.
Apply Gen₂ and combine this inequality with A≤Gen₁(A) to get Gen₂LGen₁=Gen₂L.
Regularity gives im K(a)=L(im a), proving the slice square.
The inclusion of each image in its closure is the natural comparison; uniqueness through monomorphisms proves naturality.
For closed B, LRB≤B and the displayed inequality give LGen₁(RB)≤B; adjunction and extensivity make RB closed and yield the restricted adjunction.

results.title: Free first-order adjunction
results.label: thm:free-first-order-adjunction
results.statement:
\label{thm:free-first-order-adjunction}
Under the syntax, derivation, and partial-inverse hypotheses of
this subsection, $\Sigma_{\mathrm{FO}}$ and $J_{\mathrm{FO}}$ are functors with
\[
 \Sigma_{\mathrm{FO}}:
 \mathsf{Pair}_c(\mathcal D)\rightleftarrows
 \mathsf{FO}_V(\mathcal D):J_{\mathrm{FO}},\qquad
 \Sigma_{\mathrm{FO}}\dashv J_{\mathrm{FO}}.
\]
The unit at $(X,a,b)$ is $\theta_X$. The counit at $(P,T)$
interprets the nullary predicate indexed by a sentence of $P$
as that sentence.
results.proof:
A pair morphism $f:(X,a,b)\to(S_P,T,\nu_P^*T)$ interprets the
nullary predicates by the closed sentences $f:X\to S_P$ and
the variables by $V\to\Tm_P$. Initiality of the free syntax
gives a unique term and formula interpretation $\widehat f$.
Since the images of the predicates are closed, induction proves
preservation of free variables, admissibility, and substitution.
The logical constructors and rule side conditions are therefore
preserved. The pair inequalities put the image of $A_{a,b}$
inside $T$, so Theorem~\ref{thm:translation-galois} gives
$\widehat f_!T_{a,b}\leq T$.

Conversely, restriction of a theory morphism along $\theta_X$
gives these pair inequalities. Uniqueness of the syntax interpretations makes the two
assignments inverse and natural. It also proves identity and
composition preservation of both functors.
To verify that $J_{\mathrm{FO}}$ takes values in
$\mathsf{Pair}_c(\mathcal D)$, interpret the free predicates
indexed by $S_P$ as their indexing sentences. The inverse image
of $T$ is a consistent closed theory containing the positive
axioms indexed by $T$ and negative axioms indexed by $\nu_P^*T$.
Its generated subtheory is consistent. Thus the required object
condition holds.
hypotheses_used: All monos have partial inverses; decidable variable object; free nullary-predicate syntax and derivation constructions for every coefficient object X; consistency conditions defining the two categories.
proof_reconstruction: A pair morphism f:X→S_P uniquely interprets the nullary predicates by closed sentences and variables identically.
Syntax initiality and induction preserve free variables, admissibility, substitution, and logical rules; the pair bounds put the generated axioms into T.
Restricting a logical translation to θ_X recovers f, giving inverse hom-set assignments.
Uniqueness gives naturality, functor laws, the displayed unit and counit.
For J_FO to land in Pair_c, interpretation of each sentence-indexed predicate as that sentence pulls a consistent closed theory back to one containing both signed axiom families.

results.label: cor:signed-first-order-incompleteness
results.statement:
\label{cor:signed-first-order-incompleteness}
Under the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:free-first-order-adjunction}, let $a,b$ be
disjoint subobjects of $X$ and suppose $T_{a,b}$ is consistent.
Then $T_{a,b}$ is essentially incomplete if and only if $(a,b)$
is inseparable in $\mathscr S$.
results.proof:
The atomic map $\theta_X$ reduces $(a,b)$ to the theorem and
refutation subobjects of $T_{a,b}$.
Corollary~\ref{cor:domain-incompleteness} proves essential
incompleteness when the pair is inseparable.

Conversely, a separator is equivalently a total $d:X\to\Two$
with value $\mathbf{t}$ on $a$ and $\mathbf{f}$ on $b$, where
$\mathbf{t},\mathbf{f}:1\to\Two$ are the coproduct injections.
Interpret the nullary predicates by $d$, equality by
$\mathbf{t}$, negation and implication by their Boolean truth
functions, and quantification by $V\times\Two\to\Two$.
Free syntax gives a total valuation $v:\Phi_X\to\Two$.
Induction gives
$v(\varphi[x:=t])=v(\varphi)$ whenever substitution is admissible.
The instantiation and equality schemes therefore have value
$\mathbf{t}$, and the quantifier distribution scheme does also.
The propositional schemes and both inference rules preserve
truth. Hence the inverse image of $\mathbf{t}$ along
$v j_X:S_X\to\Two$ is a closed, consistent, complete sentence
theory containing $A_{a,b}$ and therefore $T_{a,b}$.
This contradicts essential incompleteness.
hypotheses_used: Free-theory hypotheses; disjoint pair; generated free signed theory consistent.
proof_reconstruction: The atomic inclusion reduces the pair to the theorem and refutation subobjects, so Corollary 4.3 proves the forward implication from inseparability.
A complementary separator gives a total Boolean map d:X→2 by the extensive coproduct decomposition.
Assign equality true, nullary predicates d, quantification the projection, and logical operations their Boolean truth functions.
Structural induction makes valuation invariant under admissible substitution; every logical axiom and rule preserves truth.
The true fiber is therefore a consistent complete extension, contradicting essential incompleteness when the pair is separable.

results.title: Turing structure in partial slices
results.label: lem:partial-slice-turing
results.statement:
\label{lem:partial-slice-turing}
Under these assumptions, $\mathscr C$ and every $\mathscr C[T]$ are
Turing categories. If $Q$ is the original Turing object, with
$\tau:Q\times Q\rightharpoonup Q$, the Turing object in $\mathscr C[T]$
is $T\times Q\to T$, with Turing morphism $1_T\times\tau$.
Let $\mathscr R[T]$ be the full restriction subcategory on the objects
$T\times X\to T$ for $X\in\mathscr R$. Then $\mathscr R[T]$ is a
recursion category and
\[
 \Split(\mathscr R[T])\simeq\mathscr C[T].
\]
results.proof:
The terminal object of $\mathcal D$ is restriction terminal in
$\mathscr C$. For $f:X\rightharpoonup Y$, split $\bar f=mr$.
The total morphism $fm$ satisfies $!_Yfm=!_Xm$, so composition with
$r$ gives $!_Yf=!_X\bar f$.

Every split object $(X,e)$ has a total embedding into $(X,1_X)$
and a partial retraction. An isomorphism $X\cong Q$ in $\mathscr R$
makes it a retract of $Q$. If
$f=\tau(a\times1_Q)$ represents a computation on $(X,e)\times Q$,
then $f=\tau((ae)\times1_Q)$ and $ae:(X,e)\to Q$ is total.
Thus $\mathscr C$ is Turing.

For $p:X\to T$, a total embedding $m_X:X\to Q$ gives a monomorphism
$\langle p,m_X\rangle:X\hookrightarrow T\times Q$, whose partial
inverse is a retraction over $T$. A computation over $T$ with source
$X\times Q\to T$ and target $T\times Q\to T$ is determined by a
partial component $f:X\times Q\rightharpoonup Q$.
Choose total $a:X\to Q$ with $f=\tau(a\times1_Q)$.
The total parameter over $T$ is $\langle p,a\rangle$.
This proves the slice Turing property.

The objects of $\mathscr R[T]$ are isomorphic and closed under binary
restriction products. Their zeros satisfy the prodominical identity,
and the same parameterization proves the Turing property.
Every object of $\mathscr C[T]$ is a retract of $T\times Q\to T$
by a total embedding, so splitting $\mathscr R[T]$ gives $\mathscr C[T]$.
hypotheses_used: R recursion category; C=Split(R); D=Tot(C) regular extensive; every D-mono has partial inverse in C.
proof_reconstruction: D’s terminal object is restriction terminal in C by splitting the domain of each partial map; binary restriction products are inherited.
For X=(X₀,e), extend f:X×Q⇀Q to its underlying R-morphism X₀×Q⇀Q, parameterize by total a₀:X₀→Q, and restrict to a₀e, total on X.
For p:X→T, the total mono ⟨p,m_X⟩:X↪T×Q has a partial inverse over T.
A partial slice computation p×_TQ_T→Q_T has Q-component f:X×Q⇀Q; its total code a:X→Q gives parameter ⟨p,a⟩:p→Q_T and evaluation 1_T×τ.

For source T×X with X∈R the parameter may depend on both t and x; full R[T] contains it. Its objects are isomorphic, product-closed and prodominical; every partial-slice object is a restriction retract of Q_T, giving the split-completion equivalence.

results.title: Theory extensions and associated categories
results.label: thm:theory-extension
results.statement:
\label{thm:theory-extension}
Let $\mathscr R,\mathscr C,\mathcal D$ and the deductive system
satisfy the preceding assumptions. For internal theories
$t:T\hookrightarrow S$ and $u:U\hookrightarrow S$, let
$i:T\hookrightarrow U$ satisfy $t=ui$. Postcomposition defines a
fully faithful restriction functor
\[
 \Sigma_i:\mathscr C[T]\longrightarrow\mathscr C[U].
\]
Pullback defines $i^*:\mathscr C[U]\to\mathscr C[T]$, and the
underlying categories have adjunctions
\[
 \Sigma_i\dashv i^*\dashv\Sigma_i.
\]
If $i$ is proper, $\Sigma_i$ is not essentially surjective.
For composable theory inclusions $i,j$,
$\Sigma_j\Sigma_i=\Sigma_{ji}$.

The sentence and theorem comparison morphisms in $\mathcal D/U$
are $i\times1_S$ and $i\times i$. They give the commutative square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
 \Sigma_i(T\times T\to T)
   \arrow[r,"i\times i"]\arrow[d,hook,"\Sigma_i\widetilde t"'] &
 (U\times U\to U)\arrow[d,hook,"\widetilde u"]\\
 \Sigma_i\widetilde S_T\arrow[r,"i\times1_S"'] & \widetilde S_U.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Equivalently, $\widetilde S_T\cong i^*\widetilde S_U$ and
$\widetilde t\leq i^*\widetilde u$.
results.proof:
Postcomposition sends $p:X\to T$ to $ip:X\to U$ and retains each
span. Monicity of $i$ makes commutation over $U$ equivalent to
commutation over $T$ for spans between such objects. This proves full
faithfulness, restriction preservation, and the composition law.

For $p:X\to T$ and $q:Y\to U$, a span from $\Sigma_i p$ to $q$
factors its right leg uniquely through $T\times_UY$. This gives
\[
 \mathscr C[U](\Sigma_i p,q)\cong\mathscr C[T](p,i^*q).
\]
A span in the reverse direction factors its monic left leg through
$T\times_UY$. Conversely, the projection $T\times_UY\to Y$ is
monic, so it preserves monic left legs under composition.
These inverse assignments give
\[
 \mathscr C[T](i^*q,p)\cong\mathscr C[U](q,\Sigma_i p).
\]
Both assignments commute with pullback composition. They are natural,
and prove the adjunctions. The unit of the second adjunction at $q$
is the partial identity with domain $T\times_UY\hookrightarrow Y$.

Every image object factors through $i$. If $1_U:U\to U$ were
isomorphic to one, $1_U$ would factor through $i$. A monic split
epimorphism is an isomorphism, proving properness.
The comparison identity
$(1_U\times u)(i\times i)=(i\times1_S)(1_T\times t)$
follows from $ui=t$. Pullback of the sentence family gives $T\times S$,
and its theorem family contains $T\times T$ by $1_T\times i$.
hypotheses_used: Monic theory inclusion i:T↪U; partial-map slice categories; pullbacks; preceding Turing setup only for their identification with split recursion categories.
proof_reconstruction: Monicity of i makes a span between postcomposed objects commute over U iff it commutes over T, proving full faithfulness.
A span from Σ_i p to q factors its right leg through the pullback, giving Σ_i⊣i*.
A span from q to Σ_i p factors its monic left leg through the same pullback, giving i*⊣Σ_i; its unit has exactly that partial domain.
The assignments commute with pullback composition, hence are natural.
An isomorphism from 1_U to an image object would make i split epic and thus invertible; the square and composition law follow from ui=t.

results.title: Incompleteness in an associated category
results.label: thm:associated-incompleteness
results.statement:
\label{thm:associated-incompleteness}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:theory-extension} and the
factorization hypothesis on $\lambda$, let $u:U\hookrightarrow S$
be a consistent internal sentence theory. Then $u$ is essentially
incomplete in $\mathscr C$ if and only if $\widetilde u=B_U(u)$ is
essentially incomplete in $\mathscr C[U]$. Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 u\text{ is incomplete}
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \widetilde\delta_u\text{ is not total},\\
 (u,\nu^*u)\text{ is inseparable in }\mathscr C
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \widetilde\delta_u\text{ has no total extension in }\mathscr C[U].
\end{aligned}
\]
If a consistent theory $t:T\hookrightarrow S$ admits a total reduction
of an inseparable pair to its theorem and refutation subobjects, every
consistent extension $u\geq t$ has an essentially incomplete theory
$\widetilde u$ in its associated category. The partial morphism $\widetilde\delta_u$ has no total extension.
results.proof:
Products with $U$ and pullback along $\lambda_U$ preserve the finite
limits, images, and finite coproducts used for consistency and
completeness. They also preserve closed theories for the indicated
calculi. Let $v$ be a closed sentence theory in the domain of either
functor, and let $C(v)$ be its closed formula subobject. Preservation
of the finite rule diagrams gives a rule algebra on the image of
$C(v)$ containing the image of the axioms $v$. The initial derivation
algebra for these image axioms maps to that rule algebra, so its
conclusion morphism factors through the image of $C(v)$. Taking
images and restricting to sentences proves that the image of $v$
is closed. This uses the assumed deduction construction in the
slice when $v$ is a theory over $U$.

A consistent complete extension of $u$ therefore gives one of $B_U(u)$
by $B_U$, and such an extension of $B_U(u)$ gives one of $u$ by $E_U$.
The isomorphism $E_UB_U\cong1$ identifies the base theory with $u$.
This proves the essential-incompleteness equivalence.

The same retraction proves that $\delta_u$ is total exactly when
$B_U(\delta_u)$ is total. By definition, $\delta_u$ is total exactly
when $u$ is complete. A total extension of $\delta_u$ is exactly a
separator of its theorem and refutation subobjects. Either functor
carries a total extension to a total extension. The retraction therefore
proves the second equivalence.
Finally, Corollary~\ref{cor:domain-incompleteness} makes the theorem and
refutation subobjects of every consistent extension of $t$ inseparable.
Apply the two equivalences just proved.
hypotheses_used: Regular extensive D; partial-map identification; parameterized syntax/derivation construction in every slice; global λ:1→S factors through each relevant theory; u consistent.
proof_reconstruction: B_U=U×− and E_U=λ_U* preserve finite limits, regular images and finite coproducts in the displayed source and target slice categories.
Applying these functors to a closed formula subobject gives a rule algebra containing the transported axioms; initiality implies the transported sentence theory is closed.
They preserve consistency/completeness, while E_UB_U≅1, so consistent complete extensions transfer both ways.
The same retraction reflects totality and transfers total extensions of δ_u; total Boolean extensions correspond exactly to complementary separators.
Corollary 4.3 supplies inseparability for each consistent extension of a base theory admitting the given reduction.

results.label: lem:arithmetized-evaluation
results.statement:
\label{lem:arithmetized-evaluation}
For this computation coding, there are an index $u\in\N$ and
primitive-recursive functions
$\operatorname{s},\operatorname{comp}:\N^2\to\N$
such that PA proves functionality
of $G$ and the universal closures of
\begin{align}
 G_u(\langle e,x\rangle,y)
   &\leftrightarrow G(e,x,y),
   \label{eq:arithmetized-universal}\\
 G(\operatorname{s}(e,a),x,y)
   &\leftrightarrow G(e,\langle a,x\rangle,y),
   \label{eq:arithmetized-specialization}\\
 G(\operatorname{comp}(f,e),x,z)
   &\leftrightarrow
     \exists y\,\bigl(G(e,x,y)\land G(f,y,z)\bigr).
   \label{eq:composition}
\end{align}
Regard $u$ as an element of $\mathcal I(\omega\times\omega,\omega)$.
For each fixed $e\in\N$, there is an index
$k_e\in\N$ for which PA proves
\[
 \forall a\forall p\,
 \bigl(G_{k_e}(a,p)\leftrightarrow
       p=\operatorname{s}(\bar e,a)\bigr).
\]
In particular, PA proves $\forall a\exists!p\,G_{k_e}(a,p)$.
explicit_hypotheses: deterministic Kleene trace coding with PA representations
reconstruction: Determinism proves functionality in PA.
Formalized universal simulation, specialization and composition supply the three graph equivalences.
PA-provable inverse coding equations transport from the cited coding to the chosen pairing.
For fixed e, the primitive-recursive function a↦s(e,a) has a PA-provably total representing index.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Determinism is needed for functionality; formalized parameterization is needed for total parameter morphisms.
The last conclusion quantifies over each fixed standard index e, not over an arbitrary external family of codes.

results.label: lem:syntactic-functional-search
results.statement:
\label{lem:syntactic-functional-search}
For every $\Sigma_1$ formula $\Gamma(x,y)$ there is an index
$a_\Gamma$ such that PA proves
\begin{gather*}
 \forall x\forall y\,
   \bigl(G_{a_\Gamma}(x,y)\longrightarrow\Gamma(x,y)\bigr),\\
 \forall x\,
   \bigl(\exists y\,G_{a_\Gamma}(x,y)
          \longleftrightarrow\exists y\,\Gamma(x,y)\bigr).
\end{gather*}
If $T$ proves that $\Gamma$ is functional, then
\[
 T\vdash\forall x\forall y\,
       \bigl(G_{a_\Gamma}(x,y)\longleftrightarrow\Gamma(x,y)\bigr).
\]
explicit_hypotheses: T extends PA; T proves functionality only for the final equivalence
reconstruction: Normalize Γ to ∃w R with R primitive recursive.
Search paired output/witness codes in numerical order, returning the first output with R.
PA verifies both no false outputs and termination iff some witness exists.
If T proves functionality, its proof identifies any Γ-output with the one returned.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Σ₁ permits witness search and the PA verification.
T-functionality is used only in graph equality, not in existence or domain equivalence.

results.label: lem:syntactic-total-category
results.statement:
\label{lem:syntactic-total-category}
There is an equivalence $\mathcal P_T\simeq\mathcal B_T$.
The category $\mathcal B_T$ is regular, with finite coproducts
that are disjoint and stable under pullback. Every monomorphism
of $\mathcal B_T$ has a partial inverse in $\Split(S_T)$.
For $\Gamma:C\to D$ in the predicate presentation, its regular
image is represented by the inclusion
\[
 R_\Gamma(y)\equiv\exists x\,\Gamma(x,y)
 \quad\hookrightarrow\quad D(y).
\]
In particular, every subobject of a predicate $D$ is isomorphic
over $D$ to an inclusion of a $\Sigma_1$ predicate.
explicit_hypotheses: T is a consistent extension of PA in the surrounding section
morphisms are Σ₁ functional graphs with T-provable support and totality
reconstruction: Witness search sends a predicate graph to the corresponding total split morphism; inverse interpretation proves full faithfulness, and coding all original objects by ω proves essential surjectivity.
Explicit predicate products and equalizers give finite limits. A provably surjective morphism has a witness-search section and hence is the coequalizer of its kernel pair.
Image predicates give regular epi–mono factorizations, with pullback stability. Parity gives disjoint stable coproducts.
For a mono, equality of kernel-pair projections proves T-injectivity; searching its transposed graph gives its partial inverse and an isomorphism onto its predicate image.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Graph equality is universal T-provability throughout.
Σ₁ and provable totality justify the searches; no standard soundness of T is used.
Consistency is not needed in these construction steps beyond the surrounding nontrivial source framework.

results.label: lem:st-finite-sigma1
results.statement:
\label{lem:st-finite-sigma1}
Let $C(x)$ be $\Sigma_1$, and let $a$ code a finite sequence with
entries $a_i$. The assertion that all entries satisfy $C$ is equivalent
in $\mathrm{PA}$ to a $\Sigma_1$ formula. The same holds, for a positive
integer $s$, for $\Sigma_1$ formulas
$D_0(x),\ldots,D_{s-1}(x)$ and a primitive-recursive function
$\ell:\N\to\{0,\ldots,s-1\}$ selecting the condition
$D_{\ell(a_i)}(a_i)$ at the $i$th entry.
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed finite family with a primitive-recursive selector
reconstruction: Replace each Σ₁ membership assertion by existence of a witness for a primitive-recursive matrix.
One existentially quantified sequence stores all witnesses; its bounded component checks are primitive recursive.
PA induction on the sequence length proves existence of the witness sequence; projection proves the converse.
A finite case distinction handles the selected predicates.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Fixed finite family makes the disjunction finite; PA induction works on internal lengths, not merely standard lists.

results.label: prop:st-syntax-initiality
results.statement:
\label{prop:st-syntax-initiality}
Let $d$ be a nonnegative integer and let $V,\Sigma_k,\Pi_k$ be
objects of $\mathcal B_T$ for $0\leq k\leq d$. Powers below
denote finite products. The endofunctor
$K:\mathcal B_T^2\to\mathcal B_T^2$ defined by
\[
 K(X,Y)=\left(
 V+\coprod_{k=0}^{d}\Sigma_k\times X^k,
 X^2+\coprod_{k=0}^{d}\Pi_k\times X^k+Y+Y^2+V\times Y
 \right)
\]
has an initial algebra in $\mathcal B_T^2$, with carriers
$\Tm$ and $\Fm$. This algebra is stable
under parameters in the sense of Appendix~\ref{app:syntax-theories}: for every object $P$,
its pullback to $(\mathcal B_T/P)^2$ is initial for $K_P$.
explicit_hypotheses: arbitrary coefficient objects V,Σk,Πk in B_T
arbitrary parameter object P and arbitrary slice algebra
reconstruction: Ordered syntax codes and membership witnesses give Σ₁ carriers and constructor graphs.
For a target slice algebra, an evaluation sequence records each value and a halting computation for its operation, retaining the parameter.
Induction in T on node count proves totality, functionality and projection preservation; witness search gives the evaluation morphism.
Root decomposition gives the algebra equations, and a second induction compares it with every algebra morphism.

Target operations need only be T-provably total on their specified carriers.
Internal induction, rather than external finite-tree induction in a nonstandard model, establishes initiality in B_T.

results.label: prop:st-list-initiality
results.statement:
\label{prop:st-list-initiality}
For every object $V$ of $\mathcal B_T$, the endofunctor
$Z\mapsto1+V\times Z$ has an initial algebra stable under
parameters.

reconstruction: The predicate that every coded entry belongs to V is Σ₁ by the finite-witness lemma.
Nil and cons give the constructor algebra.
Evaluate from the tail using the target nil and cons operations, keeping one parameter value.
T-induction on length proves totality, algebra equations and uniqueness.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: T-totality of target operations suffices; no external choice or standardness premise is used.

results.label: prop:st-substitution-realization
results.statement:
\label{prop:st-substitution-realization}
On the preceding codes, the list operations, free-variable morphisms,
term substitution, and the formula-substitution morphism with codomain
$1+\Fm$ of Appendix~\ref{app:syntax-theories} are represented by algorithms whose
defining equations and preservation of the specified carriers are
provable in $\PA$. Restricting each graph to its source predicate
gives a morphism of $\mathcal B_T$. These are the morphisms
constructed there by parameterized initiality. In particular, the
subobject $\Adm$ is the free-for substitution domain on
these named-variable codes, represented by a complemented
subobject in $\mathcal B_T$.
explicit_hypotheses: syntax/list objects and their parameterized initiality
reconstruction: Primitive recursion gives concatenation, deletion, membership and free-variable lists, with PA-provable carrier and constructor equations.
A simultaneous traversal retains both the original subtree and substituted value.
The equal-binder case returns the original formula even if recursion in its body is inadmissible; the other case uses the exact capture condition.
PA induction identifies the second coproduct inverse image with the free-for domain and proves identity/absent-variable laws; initiality identifies these algorithms with the categorical morphisms.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Decidable equality drives binding and capture tests.
The source predicates guard all algorithms; no claim is made that arbitrary coefficient membership is decidable.

results.label: lem:syntactic-derivation-initiality
results.statement:
\label{lem:syntactic-derivation-initiality}
Let $T\supseteq\PA$, let $F$ be an object of $\mathcal B_T$, and
fix morphisms
\[
 p_n:R_n\longrightarrow F^n,\qquad
 q_n:R_n\longrightarrow F\qquad(0\leq n\leq N),
\]
where $N$ is a fixed nonnegative integer.
The inference endofunctor $H$ of
Appendix~\ref{app:closed-subobjects} has an initial algebra in

are represented by $\Sigma_1$ formulas.

reconstruction: Strictly increasing node coding gives primitive-recursive tree shape and ordered node occurrences.
Σ₁ node conditions validate label membership and equality of child conclusions with prescribed premises.
A target-algebra evaluation relation is functional in PA; T-induction gives totality on valid trees and the required conclusion.
Witness search produces a total slice morphism; root decomposition gives its algebra equation, and T-induction proves uniqueness among all algebra morphisms.

results.label: thm:syntactic-generated-theory
results.statement:
\label{thm:syntactic-generated-theory}
Let $T$ be a consistent extension of $\PA$ and put
$\mathcal B_T=\Tot(\Split(S_T))$. Fix a nonnegative integer $d$
and variable and signature objects $V,\Sigma_k,\Pi_k$ of
$\mathcal B_T$ for $0\leq k\leq d$.
The syntax, list, and substitution constructions above realize
the first-order structure of Appendix~\ref{app:syntax-theories}
in $\mathcal B_T$. For every axiom subobject $i_A:A\hookrightarrow S$
of its sentence object, the inference endofunctor $H_A$ has an
initial algebra with conclusion morphism $c_A:P_A\to\Fm$.
Its image is the least subobject of $\Fm$ containing the logical
and nonlogical axioms and closed under generalization and modus
ponens. The sentence pullback of this image is the least sentence
theory containing $A$.

Use the sentence predicate above, and choose the derivation
predicate $P_A(p)$ and conclusion index $e_A$ furnished by the
construction. Put $\operatorname{Th}_A(z)\equiv\exists p\,G_{e_A}(p,z)$.
Then the restriction idempotent
\[
 t_A=[\operatorname{Sent}(z)\land\operatorname{Th}_A(z)]_T:
                  \omega\rightharpoonup\omega
\]
belongs to $S_T$, and its splitting represents that sentence theory.
explicit_hypotheses: finite signature and arbitrary variable object
reconstruction: Regularity and partial inverses come from the predicate equivalence.
Parameterized syntax, lists and admissible substitution realize every finite rule source and conclusion.
The derivation initiality lemma and Appendix A image theorem yield the least closed formula object and sentence theory.
A PA-functional program for sentence-filtered conclusion has the indicated domain and range; its splitting is the regular image.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: The formula theorem predicate is intersected with Sent before being used as the sentence domain.
The carrier/predicate presentation is essential for PA-provable functionality.

results.label: prop:model
results.statement:
\label{prop:model}
For every $M\models T$, \eqref{eq:model-functor} defines a covariant
functor $F_M:S_T\to\Pfn$ preserving restrictions, zeros, binary
restriction products and coproducts, ranges, and finite joins of
restriction idempotents.

reconstruction: Functionality makes each interpreted graph a partial function.
Provable graph equality makes the assignment well defined on classes; composition uses all M-elements as intermediate codes and the coding bijection.
Existential domain/range predicates interpret exactly as set-theoretic domain and image.
Predicate conjunction/disjunction and program product/coproduct equations give the remaining preservation claims.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Standard index numerals are distinguished from possibly nonstandard trace and value witnesses.
No claim is made that these interpreted partial functions are computable in the standard sense.

results.label: lem:switch
results.statement:
\label{lem:switch}
Let $c,c'$ be complementary restriction idempotents on $X$ in $S_T$.
There is a total morphism $s:X\to X+X$ with
\[
 sc=i_1c,\qquad sc'=i_0c'.
\]
For every $M\models T$, the morphism $\chi_{X,X}^{-1}F_Ms$ is the
unique section of $\nabla_{F_MX}(F_Mc'+F_Mc)$, where
$\chi_{X,X}:F_MX+F_MX\to F_M(X+X)$ is the coproduct isomorphism.

reconstruction: Σ₁ predicates for c,c′ are T-provably disjoint and cover the input.
The even/odd conditional relation is thus T-functional and total; witness search gives a total source morphism.
In M it chooses the required summand and is the partial inverse of the codiagonal restricted to c′+c.
That restricted map is an injection onto the whole target, proving uniqueness of the section.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Complementarity supplies both totality and uniqueness; source totality is T-provable.

results.label: cor:model-pair
results.statement:
\label{cor:model-pair}
For every $M\models T$, the functor $F_M$ satisfies the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:source-conditionals}. Thus, for a Turing morphism
$\tau:\omega\times\omega\rightharpoonup\omega$ and an isomorphism
$b:\omega\to\omega+\omega$ in $S_T$, the restriction idempotents
\[
 (b\tau\Delta_\omega)^*(1_\omega+0_\omega),\qquad
 (b\tau\Delta_\omega)^*(0_\omega+1_\omega)
\]
are inseparable in $S_T$.
explicit_hypotheses: τ is a Turing morphism and b:ω≅ω+ω
reconstruction: The model functor preserves the required structures.
Set-theoretic total inverse images preserve joins, and M is nonempty.
The previous lemma supplies all complementary source conditionals.
Corollary3.3 yields inseparability of the two diagonal source domains.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Nonempty M witnesses F(1ω)≠0.
The argument proves source inseparability, not inseparability of the image pair in Pfn.

results.label: prop:model-total-regular
reconstruction: Work in the predicate presentation: terminal, product and equalizer predicates interpret as the corresponding set limits.
Parity identifies the interpreted coproduct with the disjoint union.
The existential image predicate interprets as the actual image because its witnesses range over all of M.
Transport along the equivalence proves the assertion for G_M.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: The claim concerns total maps; no preservation of partial-map Turing universality is inferred.

results.label: lem:semantic-substitution
results.statement:
\label{lem:semantic-substitution}
Let $\sigma:\N\to |K|$ be an assignment of values to variables.
For $x\in\N$ and $a\in|K|$, write
$\sigma[x\mapsto a]:\N\to|K|$ for the assignment obtained
by changing the value of $x$ to $a$. For finite terms $r,t$,
\[
 \llbracket r[x:=t]\rrbracket^K_\sigma
 =\llbracket r\rrbracket^K_{
          \sigma[x\mapsto\llbracket t\rrbracket^K_\sigma]}.
\]
For a finite formula $\varphi$, if
$(\ulcorner\varphi\urcorner,x,\ulcorner t\urcorner)$ lies in
the image of $a_{\N}$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:semantic-substitution}
 K,\sigma\models\varphi[x:=t]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 K,\sigma[x\mapsto\llbracket t\rrbracket^K_\sigma]
             \models\varphi.
\end{equation}
The substitution morphisms of
Proposition~\ref{prop:st-substitution-realization}, interpreted by
$G_{\N}$, give the codes of $r[x:=t]$ and, when admissible,
$\varphi[x:=t]$.
explicit_hypotheses: K a nonempty first-order structure with identity equality
the displayed formula substitution is admissible
reconstruction: Simultaneous induction establishes dependence only on free-variable values.
Term substitution follows by constructor induction.
For ∀y, y=x leaves the formula unchanged; when y≠x and x occurs, admissibility ensures y is absent from t, so updated assignments commute.
Quantification then yields the formula equivalence; realized constructor equations identify the codes.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Admissibility is used exactly in the capture-sensitive quantifier case.
The induction is on external finite syntax interpreted by G_N, not on nonstandard syntax.

results.label: prop:standard-code-soundness
results.statement:
\label{prop:standard-code-soundness}
Let $\Gamma$ be a computably enumerable set of arithmetic sentences,
with axiom subobject $i_A:A\hookrightarrow S$ in
$\mathcal B_{\PA}$, and let $K\models\Gamma$.
There is a unique function
\[
 e_K:G_{\N}P_{A,S}\longrightarrow V_K
 \quad\text{such that}\quad
 v_Ke_K=G_{\N}c_{A,S}.
\]
If $\nu:S\to S$ is sentence negation, then the subobjects
$v_K$ and $(G_{\N}\nu)^*v_K$ of $G_{\N}S$ have empty
intersection.
explicit_hypotheses: K models Γ with identity equality
G_N interpretation of the chosen finite derivation codes
reconstruction: The three propositional and four quantifier/equality schemes are valid under every assignment.
Nonlogical axioms are sentences true in K; modus ponens and unrestricted generalization preserve validity.
Induction on the externally finite derivation yields a conclusion in V_K.
Corestriction gives the unique function e_K, and negation semantics proves disjointness.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: N interprets syntax and program graphs; K interprets decoded formulas.
No arithmetic axioms of K are needed for the pure logical soundness step.

results.label: lem:ultrapower-regular
reconstruction: Coordinate pairing gives products; for an equalizing class, the set of coordinates in the equalizer is U-large.
Fill the complement with one equalizer element to obtain a representative in that subobject.
The ultrafilter chooses exactly one coproduct summand; fill its complement to get coproduct surjectivity, and disjointness gives injectivity.
A section of each set surjection survives functoriality, so image factorizations are preserved.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Properness makes every U-large set nonempty; ultrafilter maximality is used for the two summands.
Choice is used for sections of arbitrary surjections.

results.label: lem:ultrapower-comparison
results.statement:
\label{lem:ultrapower-comparison}
There is a natural isomorphism of functors
\[
 \eta:\mathscr U G_{\N}\xRightarrow{\ \cong\ }G_M:
             \mathcal B_{\PA}\longrightarrow\mathbf{Set}.
\]
On a predicate object $J_{\PA}(C)$ it is the map
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ultrapower-predicate-comparison}
 \eta_{J_{\PA}(C)}:
 \mathscr U(C(\N))\longrightarrow C(M),
 \qquad [c_i]\longmapsto[c_i].
\end{equation}
reconstruction: A family of C(N)-elements maps to its arithmetic class in C(M).
Łoś proves injectivity; if a class satisfies C, replace its coordinates outside the U-large satisfaction set by a satisfying value.
Interpreted functional graphs give the naturality square.
Transport by predicate-presentation isomorphisms extends uniquely to B_PA and proves independence of those choices.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Empty C(N) is handled explicitly.
The comparison is between internal arithmetic predicates and ultrapowers of their standard carriers, not a decoding of nonstandard formulas.

results.label: thm:ultrapower-soundness
results.statement:
\label{thm:ultrapower-soundness}
Let $i_A:A\hookrightarrow S$ and $K$ satisfy the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:standard-code-soundness}, and let
$\nu:S\to S$ be syntactic negation in $\mathcal B_{\PA}$.
Let $I$ be nonempty,
let $\mathcal U$ be a proper ultrafilter on $I$, and put
$M=\N^I/\mathcal U$. Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_{K,\mathcal U}&=\mathscr U(V_K),\\
 v_{K,\mathcal U}
   &=\eta_S\mathscr U(v_K):V_{K,\mathcal U}\hookrightarrow G_MS,\\
 e_{K,\mathcal U}
   &=\mathscr U(e_K)\eta_{P_{A,S}}^{-1}:
       G_MP_{A,S}\longrightarrow V_{K,\mathcal U}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ultrapower-soundness-factorization}
 v_{K,\mathcal U}e_{K,\mathcal U}=G_Mc_{A,S},
\end{equation}
and $v_{K,\mathcal U}$ has empty intersection with its inverse
image along $G_M\nu$. Consequently the interpreted theorem
subobject and its inverse image along $G_M\nu$ have empty
intersection. Equivalently, for the restriction idempotent
$t_A=\ran(c_{A,S})$ in $\Split(S_{\PA})$,
\[
 \widehat F_M(t_A)\,
       (\widehat F_M\nu)^*\widehat F_M(t_A)=0.
\]
explicit_hypotheses: standard-code soundness for Γ in K
reconstruction: Apply the ultrapower functor to the standard soundness factorization.
Naturality of η identifies its composite with the M-interpreted conclusion.
Preservation of the empty intersection and naturality for negation transfer disjointness.
Regular-image preservation identifies the conclusion image with the interpreted theorem domain, proving both consistency formulations.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: K is unchanged and need not be an ultrapower; M interprets code objects only.
No external semantic interpretation of a nonstandard formula is asserted.

results.label: lem:arithmetic-diagonal-representation
results.statement:
\label{lem:arithmetic-diagonal-representation}
There is a total morphism
$\theta:\omega\to S$ in $\mathcal B_{\PA}$ such that
$(G_{\N}\theta)(n)=\ulcorner\alpha(\bar n)\urcorner$.
Suppose that every axiom of PA is derivable from the c.e.\
sentence set $\Gamma$. For every $M\equiv\N$, the following
inequalities hold in $\Pfn$:
\begin{align*}
 F_M(a_0)&\le
   (\widehat F_M\theta)^*\widehat F_M(t_\Gamma),\\
 F_M(a_1)&\le
   (\widehat F_M\theta)^*(\widehat F_M\nu)^*
                   \widehat F_M(t_\Gamma).
\end{align*}
explicit_hypotheses: Γ c.e. and derives every PA axiom
reconstruction: Numeral construction and substitution in fixed α give a PA-total sentence-code morphism θ.
A standard halting trace proves α(n), or proves β(n) and hence ¬α(n), in PA.
Only finitely many PA axioms are used, so Γ derives these sentences.
The two universal reduction implications are true in N and therefore in every M≡N; interpreted image and inverse-image formulas give the inequalities.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: The reduction implications are asserted true in N, not PA-provable uniformly from an external claim that Γ extends PA.
Elementary equivalence, stronger than M⊨PA, is used to transport those implications.

results.label: lem:arithmetic-proof-search
results.statement:
\label{lem:arithmetic-proof-search}
For every c.e.\ sentence set $\Gamma$, there is a morphism
$\ell_\Gamma:\omega\rightharpoonup\omega+\omega$ in
$S_{\PA}$ with the following property. In any $M\models\PA$
for which
\[
 C(x)=\operatorname{Prov}_\Gamma(\Theta(x)),\qquad
 C'(x)=\operatorname{Prov}_\Gamma(\operatorname{Neg}(\Theta(x)))
\]
have disjoint truth sets, the partial function
\[
 s_\Gamma=\chi_{\omega,\omega}^{-1}F_M(\ell_\Gamma):
       F_M\omega\rightharpoonup F_M\omega+F_M\omega
\]
in $\Pfn$ satisfies
\[
 s_\Gamma^*(1_{F_M\omega}+0_{F_M\omega})=[C'(M)],\qquad
 s_\Gamma^*(0_{F_M\omega}+1_{F_M\omega})=[C(M)].
\]
Here $[C(M)]$ denotes the partial identity on
$\{x\in M:M\models C(x)\}$, and $[C'(M)]$ is defined in the
same way.
explicit_hypotheses: C and C′ have disjoint truth sets in M
reconstruction: One Σ₁ search relation requests an odd output for C and an even output for C′.
Witness search supplies a source index with the exact union domain and only valid outputs.
In M, disjointness makes the requested relation functional.
Existence plus functionality forces its graph to be exactly that relation, yielding the two inverse-image equations.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: No PA proof of Γ-consistency is assumed.
The source lift may be partial; disjointness is a target-model hypothesis.

results.label: thm:arithmetic-internal-comparison
results.statement:
\label{thm:arithmetic-internal-comparison}
Let $\Gamma$ be a consistent c.e.\ set of arithmetic sentences
from which every PA-axiom is derivable. Its sentence theory
$t_\Gamma$ in $\Split(S_{\PA})$ is incomplete.
Its interpretations under $\widehat F_{\N}$ and under every
$\widehat F_M$, where $M=\N^I/\mathcal U$ for a proper ultrafilter
$\mathcal U$ on a nonempty set $I$, are incomplete.
For the standard interpretation, there is a total morphism
$g:\omega\to\omega$ in $S_{\PA}$ such that, writing
$\gamma=F_{\N}(g):\N\to\N$, every sentence
$\alpha(\overline{\gamma(n)})$ is undecidable from $\Gamma$.
explicit_hypotheses: Γ consistent c.e. sentences deriving all PA axioms
M=N or an arithmetic ultrapower of N
reconstruction: Completeness gives K⊨Γ. Standard-code soundness and ultrapower transport make the target theorem/refutation domains disjoint.
The diagonal representation supplies reductions and the search lemma supplies the required partial source lift.
The comparison theorem yields noncoverage in the target and source.
For N, the resulting single total source g supplies undecidable sentences at every input via Θ.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Consistency is external and yields a model; no internal Cons(Γ) proof is assumed.
Each arithmetic ultrapower is elementarily equivalent to N, as the reduction lemma requires.

results.label: cor:arithmetic
explicit_hypotheses: Γ consistent c.e. extension of PA
standard recursive separator assumed for contradiction
reconstruction: Pull the separator of theorem/refutation codes back along recursive Θ.
The diagonal reductions make it separate D0,D1. Its total recursive reversed conditional has a source program index.
Corollary3.2 contradicts the existence of that lifted separator.
A consistent complete c.e. extension would have disjoint c.e. theorem/refutation sets deciding sentence membership and hence give the forbidden separator.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: All separator effectiveness is standard, with no claim of PA-provable totality for arbitrary recursive decisions.
The code outside the recursive sentence carrier is assigned false.

results.label: prop:arithmetic-theory-fibers
results.statement:
\label{prop:arithmetic-theory-fibers}
For every $e\in\N$, the pullback of $c^{\mathrm{all}}$ along
$k_e^{\Fm}$ is the underlying conclusion morphism of an initial
$H_{A_{\Gamma_e}}$-algebra in $\mathcal B/\Fm$.
There is an induced morphism $\iota_e:P_{\Gamma_e}\to P$
in $\mathcal B$, and the square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
 P_{\Gamma_e}\arrow[r,"\iota_e"]
       \arrow[d,"c_{\Gamma_e}"'] & P\arrow[d,"c"]\\
 S\arrow[r,"k_e^S"'] & E\times S
\end{tikzcd}
\]
is a pullback in $\mathcal B$. Consequently
$(k_e^S)^*m$ is the sentence theory generated by $A_{\Gamma_e}$.
explicit_hypotheses: rules retain a common E coordinate
reconstruction: The numeral fiber and its decidable complement split E and induce an equivalence of the two slice categories.
Rule sources and conclusions decompose under that equivalence; pullback pasting gives a natural isomorphism of inference endofunctors.
Consequently their algebra categories decompose. The initial pair has an initial first component, by pairing every comparison with the identity of the second.
Taking sentence pullbacks and stable regular images gives the square and theory fiber.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: The proof establishes initiality after reindexing rather than assuming arbitrary pullback preserves initial algebras.
Only standard numeral e is used, and its complement is explicitly available.

results.label: thm:uniform-independent-sentences
results.statement:
\label{thm:uniform-independent-sentences}
For the family $\Gamma_e$ and objects
$E,S\in\mathcal B=\Tot(\Split(S_{\PA}))$ of
Section~\ref{subsec:indexed-arithmetic-theories}, there is a morphism
$q:E\to S$ in $\mathcal B$ such that,
for every $e\in\N$ with $\Gamma_e$ consistent, the
sentence with code $(G_{\N}q)(e)$ is neither provable nor
refutable from $\Gamma_e$.
explicit_hypotheses: Γe is the universal c.e. family with PA axioms adjoined
consistency only of the selected Γe
reconstruction: The one family predicate Prov(e,z) gives a single Σ₁ reversed search relation R(e,x,z).
One source index for R and one Turing factorization give a total g before e and its consistency proof are chosen.
At n=F_N(g)(e), the identity hg=ℓ⟨1,g⟩ turns either provability alternative into the opposite diagonal domain.
The diagonal reductions and disjointness contradict that alternative; q=θg yields one total morphism with the required independent value.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Uniformity is constructive in the order of choices: ℓ,g,q precede every selected e.
Consistency is used only to establish target disjointness, not to produce g.
The PA-provable numeral-fiber comparison equates Prov(e,−) with the selected presentation.

results.label: prop:numerical-structure
results.statement:
\label{prop:numerical-structure}
There is an equivalence
\[
 \operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Split}(\mathrm{Rec}))
       \simeq\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}.
\]
The category $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}$ is regular, with finite
coproducts that are disjoint and stable under pullback. Under the
displayed equivalence, every monomorphism of $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}$
corresponds to a restriction monomorphism in
$\operatorname{Split}(\mathrm{Rec})$, and
\[
 \operatorname{Par}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}},\operatorname{Mono})
       \simeq\operatorname{Split}(\mathrm{Rec}).
\]
explicit_hypotheses: objects are c.e. finite-dimensional numerical carriers
total computable morphisms, with extensional equality
reconstruction: Encoding and decoding define Q and F with explicit natural isomorphisms.
Computable products/equalizers give limits; parity gives stable disjoint coproducts.
C.e. image carriers and preimage search show regular epis are surjections and monos are injections with computable partial inverses.
Monic spans correspond exactly to partial computable functions on c.e. subcarriers; explicit quasi-inverse functors and naturality prove the restriction equivalence.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Preimage searches terminate on their prescribed carrier only.
Equality of partial maps is checked by both their domains and values.

results.label: prop:arithmetic-theory-realization
results.statement:
\label{prop:arithmetic-theory-realization}
Fix $d\ge0$, let $V=(1,\N)$, and let
$\Sigma_k=(1,\Sigma_{k,0})$ and $\Pi_k=(1,\Pi_{k,0})$
have recursive carriers for $0\le k\le d$. Then the
syntax and list algebras of Definition~\ref{def:categorical-syntax}
exist in $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}$ and are stable under parameters.
For every axiom subobject of the sentence object, the inference
endofunctor of Theorem~\ref{thm:first-order-theory} has an initial
algebra of finite derivations.
explicit_hypotheses: arbitrary c.e. parameter and axiom objects
reconstruction: Recursive syntax carriers and parameter-retaining tree evaluation give initial syntax algebras in every slice.
List evaluation proves the same assertion for lists; constructor equations identify free-variable and substitution maps.
Finite rule membership and computation tests semidecide valid derivation codes.
Bottom-up evaluation in any target inference algebra is total on those codes; conclusion preservation, algebra equations and uniqueness follow by tree induction.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: Recursive signatures are used for decidability of syntax carriers; axiom membership only needs semidecision.
Totality is relative to source carriers, not total computability on all natural numbers.

results.label: lem:arithmetic-signed-theory
results.statement:
\label{lem:arithmetic-signed-theory}
Assume that $\PA$ is consistent. The pair $a_0,a_1$ is inseparable
in $\mathscr C_{\PA}$, and the internal theory $t_{\pm}$ is
consistent and essentially incomplete.
explicit_hypotheses: free first-order theory generated by the diagonal signed atoms
reconstruction: A hypothetical complementary separator in the splitting gives a source-total conditional on ω.
Turing parameterization with π2 and precomposition with ⟨1,g⟩ yield hg=ℓg and contradictory complementary pullbacks.
For two allegedly contradictory derivations, collect positive leaf labels in a finite list; make exactly those nullary predicates true, every equality true, and erase quantifiers.
PA verifies that all leaves and logical rules preserve this valuation, contradicting simultaneous truth of a formula and its negation; the signed-theory criterion gives essential incompleteness.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: PA consistency is used for 1ω≠0, not to infer internal soundness.
The valuation is computed from both derivations and its correctness is proved internally by PA induction.
Nullary predicates and equality-only terms permit quantifier erasure.

results.label: cor:arithmetic-associated-categories
results.statement:
\label{cor:arithmetic-associated-categories}
Assume that $\PA$ is consistent. Let
$u:U\hookrightarrow S^{\pm}$ be any consistent internal sentence
theory containing $t_{\pm}$, and write $t_{\pm}=ui$.
Then
\[
 \Sigma_i:
 \Par(\mathcal B_{\PA}/T_{\pm})
 \longrightarrow
 \Par(\mathcal B_{\PA}/U)
\]
is fully faithful, and is not essentially surjective when $i$ is
proper. Both categories are split Turing categories, and the
theory
\[
 1_U\times u:U\times U\hookrightarrow U\times S^{\pm}
\]
in the latter category is essentially incomplete. Its partial
Boolean morphism, true on the theorem domain and false on the
refutation domain, has no total extension.

Let $\mathscr R_{\PA}[U]$ be the full restriction subcategory of
$\Par(\mathcal B_{\PA}/U)$ on the objects
$U\times X\to U$, for $X$ in $S_{\PA}$.
It is a recursion category, with
$\Split(\mathscr R_{\PA}[U])\simeq\Par(\mathcal B_{\PA}/U)$.
The functor
\[
 S_{\PA}\longrightarrow\mathscr R_{\PA}[U],\qquad
 X\longmapsto(U\times X\to U),\qquad
 f\longmapsto1_U\times f
\]
is faithful and sends $\tau_{\PA}$ to $1_U\times\tau_{\PA}$,
a Turing morphism in $\mathscr R_{\PA}[U]$.
explicit_hypotheses: U a consistent internal extension of the signed theory
reconstruction: The PA total splitting supplies regularity, extensivity and partial mono inverses.
Parameterized syntax and derivations come from the arithmetic constructions.
The closed equality theorem gives a global point of every extension U.
Apply the extension and incompleteness theorems and the constant-family recursion-subcategory construction.
hypothesis_use_and_scope: This is the separate nullary signed theory, not the arbitrary arithmetical Γ theory of Theorem8.3.
Faithfulness is obtained from evaluation at the global theorem point.

results.label: thm:least-theorem-subobject
results.statement:
\label{thm:least-theorem-subobject}
With the rule data above, suppose
$\delta:H(P,c)\to(P,c)$ is an initial algebra in $\mathcal D/F$.
The image of its conclusion morphism $c:P\to F$ is the least
subobject of $F$ closed under the rules.
results.proof:
Factor $c=me$ with $e:P\twoheadrightarrow T$ regular epic and
$m:T\hookrightarrow F$ monic. The endofunctor $H$ preserves
regular epimorphisms: finite products preserve them in a regular
category, each $B_n(e)$ is a pullback of $e^n$, and finite coproducts
preserve coequalizers. Thus $H(e)$ is regular epic.

Writing $|H(P,c)|$ for the underlying object of the slice object,
the equations $c\delta=\kappa_c$ and
$\kappa_mH(e)=\kappa_c$ give the commuting square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large]
 \lvert H(P,c)\rvert\arrow[r,"e\delta"]\arrow[d,two heads,"H(e)"'] &
 T\arrow[d,hook,"m"]\\
 \lvert H(T,m)\rvert\arrow[r,"\kappa_m"']\arrow[ur,dashed,"\alpha"] & F.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Since $m$ is monic, $e\delta$ coequalizes the kernel pair of $H(e)$.
The regular epimorphism $H(e)$ is its kernel-pair coequalizer, so
there is a unique diagonal $\alpha$. In particular, $m\alpha=\kappa_m$,
so the image is closed. If $u:U\hookrightarrow F$ is another
closed subobject, initiality gives an algebra morphism
$v:(P,c)\to(U,u)$, hence $uv=c$. The image factorization gives
a unique $w:T\to U$ with $uw=m$.

proof_reconstruction: Factor the conclusion c=me with e regular epic.
Finite products, pullback and coproduct of coequalizers show H(e) regular epic.
The commuting square against m makes eδ coequalize the kernel pair of H(e); descend to the unique rule algebra on the image.
For every closed subobject U, initiality provides a map P→U over F; the image universal property gives T→U.
Thus the image is closed and least.

results.title: Regular images and ranges
results.label: lem:range-regular-image
results.statement:
\label{lem:range-regular-image}
Let $\mathcal S$ be a restriction category with ranges in which every
restriction idempotent splits. Suppose $\mathcal D=\Tot(\mathcal S)$
is regular, and let $f:X\to Y$ have regular-image factorization
$f=me$ in $\mathcal D$, with $e:X\twoheadrightarrow I$ and
$m:I\hookrightarrow Y$.
If $m$ has a partial inverse $r:Y\rightharpoonup I$ in $\mathcal S$,
then $\ran(f)=mr=\bar r$.
results.proof:
The restriction idempotent $mr$ receives $f$, since $mrf=mrme=f$.
Let $a:Y\rightharpoonup Y$ be any restriction idempotent receiving $f$.
Choose a splitting $a=js$, where $j:J\to Y$ is total,
$s:Y\rightharpoonup J$, and $sj=1_J$.
Then $f=j(sf)$, and $sf:X\to J$ is total, since
$\overline{sf}=\overline{jsf}=\bar f=1_X$.
The morphism $j$ is monic in $\mathcal D$, so the universal property
of the regular image gives a unique $u:I\to J$ with $ju=m$.
Consequently, $am=jsju=ju=m$ and $a(mr)=mr$.
Thus $mr\leq a$, so $mr=\ran(f)$.
hypotheses_used: S has ranges and all restriction idempotents split; D=Tot(S) regular; image mono m has partial inverse r.
proof_reconstruction: mr receives f=me.
Split any receiving restriction idempotent a=js; sf is total because j is total and jsf=f.
Since j is a total mono receiving f, the regular image factors as m=ju.
Then am=m and a(mr)=mr, proving mr is the least receiving restriction idempotent.
